clue.text: Reject plant in row

indicators.note: one thing set in another is placed inside it, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din
to plant seed is to sow it

explanation.surface: A gardener rejects a seedling set in the wrong row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a line of plants beside 'plant', but here it means a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse any connection with them, a way of casting them off.

clue.text: Proper defeat, lacking time to break fiendish codes

indicators.note: one word breaking another splits it open and sits in the gap
fiendish suggests something devilishly tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, and lacking it means that letter is removed

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat

explanation.surface: Code-breakers admit defeat against a devilish cipher in the proper manner.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUT loses its T to give ROU, which breaks into DECOS, the jumbled codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorous behaviour is seemly and in keeping with good taste and polite conduct.

clue.text: Browse, catching update finally? Anger guaranteed

indicators.note: something catching another holds it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to surf the web is to browse it

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of update
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone browsing online is bound to get angry when an update finally arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger guaranteed' looks like one phrase; only the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A surefire method is certain to succeed, so its result is guaranteed.

clue.text: Run through desert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to squander or use up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like crossing a desert on foot; 'run through' means squander, as with money.
explanation.definitionFit: You can squander money or resources, and a barren wilderness is called a wasteland or waste.

clue.text: Benefit to a smaller extent during spree, losing energy

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits inside it, so one word is held within the other
energy is abbreviated E in physics, and losing it means that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a binge is a bout of indulgence
less means to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: Advice that cutting back during a wild spree pays off, provided you lose some energy.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the standard abbreviation for energy, as in physics formulas.
explanation.definitionFit: A blessing is something advantageous or welcome, a boon that does you good.

clue.text: Racing driver revealed consuming desire and raised capital

indicators.note: something consuming others swallows them, so they go inside

parts.note: let on means revealed a secret
a wish is a desire

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom up

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: A racing driver confesses his ambition, and money is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Hamilton is the British Formula One world champion; 'raised capital' sounds like fundraising but is a city read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Hamilton is a multiple Formula One world champion, an example of a racing driver.

clue.text: Company, restricted by trees coming up, about to give signal for pause

indicators.note: something restricted by another is hemmed in by it, so it sits inside
in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom to the top

parts.note: limes are trees, also called lindens
Co is the abbreviation for company
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A firm hemmed in by woodland signals a break.
explanation.walkthrough: LIMES upside down is SEMIL, which holds CO; ON is then added.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicolon is a punctuation mark marking a pause longer than a comma's.

clue.text: Truly denied going wrong

indicators.note: something going wrong falls into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a denial has honestly gone awry.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic adverb meaning really or in fact, used to stress a statement.

clue.text: Uncertain about editor being eager

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a grey area is uncertain
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An unsure editor is nonetheless keen.
explanation.walkthrough: A grey area is a matter that is unclear, hence uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy can mean keenly desirous, as in being greedy for success, so eager.

clue.text: Opener getting frantic rocks team

indicators.note: something frantic is wild and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A sports opener who rattles the opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a batsman or the first match of a season, but it is a tool for opening bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the spiral tool used for opening wine bottles by pulling the cork.

clue.text: Crept over site nervously looking back

indicators.note: doing something nervously means jittery and unsettled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An intruder sneaks across a site, glancing anxiously behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospective describes something that surveys or concerns the past, so backward-looking.

clue.text: Fly westward for example and fade

indicators.note: in an across clue, travelling west means reading from right to left

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
to fade is to grow dim

explanation.surface: An insect flying west into the fading light.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny two-winged insect, a small gnat-like kind of fly.

clue.text: Contemplate display

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to think deeply about
second meaning: to show or express

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a command to study an exhibition; they are separate senses of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both careful thought about something and showing or mirroring something outwardly.

clue.text: Replace work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to follow someone in a post
second meaning: to turn out well, as a plan does

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to redo a job; the two words are separate senses of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: You take over from a predecessor in office, and a scheme that comes off has had the desired result.

clue.text: Excessively excited by role as a nun

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up and agitated, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: all twelve letters go into the mix

explanation.surface: An actor gets far too worked up about being cast as a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited by' looks like one phrase, but 'by' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unreasonably means going beyond sensible limits, to an excessive or immoderate degree.

clue.text: Agile graduate absorbed by word puzzle, not small

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is soaked up into it, so it goes inside
small is abbreviated S, so not small means that letter is removed

parts.note: an acrostic is a word puzzle
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A nimble graduate is engrossed in a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: An acrostic is a puzzle whose line initials spell a word; S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatic movements are nimble and gymnastic, showing great physical agility.

clue.text: Poor old weaver, left out, intimidated

indicators.note: poor suggests something in a bad state, so the letters are reworked
left is abbreviated L, and out means that letter is removed

parts.note: letters to be rearranged after the deletion

explanation.surface: A poor old weaver, left out of things, feels cowed.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD WEAVER loses its L before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Overawed means so impressed or daunted as to be subdued, hence intimidated.

clue.text: Vicious cycle stopped by people showing mercy

indicators.note: something stopped by another is plugged with it, so it goes in the middle
vicious suggests something savage and violent, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
men are people

explanation.surface: People break a vicious cycle by showing compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious cycle' reads as a set phrase, but 'vicious' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clemency is leniency shown to an offender, a synonym for mercy.

clue.text: Serious line receiving chop in silly pictorial story

indicators.note: something receiving another takes it in, so the scrambled letters go inside

parts.note: grave means serious, solemn
L is the abbreviation for line

indicators.note: silly means foolish and muddled, so the words beside it are scrambled

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grave sentence is cut up into something silly in a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop in' looks like a single action, but the two words are both the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphic novel is a book-length narrative told in comic-strip panels, a story in pictures.

clue.text: Preserve most of immense painting

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
vast means immense

explanation.surface: A conservator saves the bulk of a huge painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas is an oil painting done on that fabric, so the word stands for the picture itself.

clue.text: Merchant involved in nationwide alert

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so the letters run within the words

parts.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A trader is caught up in a national emergency warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer is a trader who buys and sells goods, so a merchant.

clue.text: Sharp expert in charge capturing rook with bishop

indicators.note: a piece capturing others takes them in, so these letters are held within

parts.note: an ace is an expert
R is the chess notation for rook
B is the chess notation for bishop
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A chess game in which a sharp player takes a rook and bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: R and B are the standard chess notation letters for those pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic remarks are cutting and biting, so sharp in the sense of harsh in tone.

clue.text: Outburst from worker perhaps with spirit after end of shift

indicators.note: the other pieces come after this one, so it is placed first
the end of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of shift
a worker is a kind of ant, hence 'perhaps'
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A worker explodes at the end of a shift, perhaps fuelled by a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A worker is a sterile ant of the colony, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an uncontrolled fit of temper, an angry outburst.

clue.text: Man under arrest not entirely in ideal position

indicators.note: not entirely means not the whole word, so its last letter is dropped
in a down clue, one piece under another simply comes after it

parts.note: nick is British slang for arrest
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man under arrest is, ironically, somewhere he feels at home.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to nick someone is to arrest them; 'under' places one piece below another in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a comfortable or suitable role, the place where someone fits best.

clue.text: Servant taking the box back full of drink

indicators.note: something full of a drink holds it within, so it goes inside
taking something back means reading it in the opposite direction

parts.note: the box is slang for television
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A servant carries the telly back after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is British slang for the television set.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant who looks after his employer's clothes and personal needs.

clue.text: Writer emerging from cinema terribly pale

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
wan means pale

explanation.surface: An author leaves a cinema looking awful, having seen an adaptation of their book.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian McEwan is the British novelist of Atonement and Amsterdam, several of whose novels have been filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian McEwan is a celebrated English novelist, so an example of a writer.

clue.text: Odds rise rapidly in projection

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the odds on a horse at the start of a race
prices that rise fast are said to rocket

explanation.surface: Betting odds shoot up as the punters forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projection' looks like a forecast to match the odds, but it is a tooth sticking out of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprocket is one of the teeth jutting from a wheel rim that engage a chain or film perforations.

clue.text: Prime fodder injected with revolutionary colourant

indicators.note: something injected with a substance has it put inside

parts.note: hay is animal fodder

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a dye is a colourant

explanation.surface: Animal feed is laced with a radical new colouring agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as radical, describing the colourant, but it signals turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Your heyday is the period of greatest success or vigour, the prime of life.
